name: Rosler Lower League Special 4-4-2

slots.why: A conventional Goalkeeper (Defend), as in the original; do not replace him with a sweeper keeper for this benchmark.
The supporting full-back narrows to cover the midfield rather than becoming an attacking wing-back.
A conventional Central Defender (Defend), matching the published setup even with Play Out Of Defence selected.
The second conventional centre-back preserves the original two-defender platform.
The right full-back also supports and tucks in behind the two supporting midfielders.
The attacking winger supplies byline deliveries while the full-back offers a supporting outside option.
The original uses Central Midfielder (Support), not a ball-winner or deep playmaker selected by the optimiser.
The other supporting central midfielder shares the running, passing and recovery load.
The right attacking winger provides the second natural wide delivery route.
The first Pressing Forward (Attack) contests the build-up and runs into the box.
The second Pressing Forward (Attack) preserves the published two-forward press and finishing presence.

description: Mr U Rosler’s FM20.3 LLS 442: two attacking pressing forwards and wingers, two supporting central midfielders, conservative full-backs and a very high, urgent defensive approach.
whyGood: Offers a documented lower-league benchmark with conventional full-backs and two strikers. The Stockport report records 98 points and 108 goals; FM-Arena’s 20.4.4 test records 67.8 points per 38 over 456 games, so lower-league success is not proof of superiority.
whyThisShape: Two central midfielders on Support provide connections and share the physical work behind two attacking wingers and two Pressing Forwards. Supporting full-backs tuck in to cover those midfielders; overlap instructions encourage consideration of their safe supporting runs, not an automatic switch to attacking wing-backs. The original uses Play Out Of Defence with two ordinary centre-backs, a deliberate exception to the catalogue’s usual ball-playing-defender preference. The very high lines, urgent pressure, Counter-Press, Counter, Get Stuck In and offside trap are retained as one published package.
whenToUse: As a practical published high-press comparison when you want to retain natural full-backs, flat wide players and two forwards, and can field midfielders who share the running and passing work.
whenNotToUse: When you cannot field two useful pressing forwards and a hard-working midfield pair, or when you need proof that a lower-league label guarantees suitability; this system still needs a local test.
whenLeading: Retain Attacking and the original settings for the fixed-policy benchmark. Any later change to mentality or tackling should be recorded as a separate version.
keyRequirements: Natural wide attackers and supporting full-backs
Keep the original player instructions and set pieces

source.author: Mr U Rosler
source.verification: Formation, roles and selected team instructions checked against FM-Arena’s screenshot of the original tactic. The unmodified FM file retains all player instructions and set-piece routines; those are not fully decoded into the catalogue. Import the original file for the benchmark.

setupNotes: Import the original .fmf using the download on this page. Keep its complete player instructions and set-piece routines for the first benchmark; the catalogue is the selection guide, not a replacement file.
Use no additional opposition instructions. Keep the starting mentality throughout the replay, and retain the same holiday management policy as the reference.
The published score describes another test environment. Assess both teams’ chances, goals, crosses and red cards with this squad before adopting it.
Standard width, passing and tempo mean no extra slider modifier relative to Attacking mentality; they do not describe slow or cautious play.
Left-back takes left corners and throw-ins; right-back takes right corners and throw-ins. Retain the downloaded routines.
Get Stuck In and the original player instructions can affect bookings. Record red cards rather than silently deleting these instructions from the benchmark.
